headline: Main target: a specific smooth hypersurface in a family where the Hodge conjecture is open, with a class proved Hodge and no known algebraic cycle ("a Hodge class not known to be algebraic"). No candidate so far. The open lead on cubic tenfolds now has an explanation by an explicit family with algebraic cycles: the cycle's self-intersection is -144 where a multiple of h^5 would have 48 (two paper arguments by an AI with mod p inputs, not yet read by a mathematician), and the family passes orders 2 and 3 exactly (mod p). If the arguments hold, the class is algebraic there; it is NOT a candidate.

headlines.title: A 1917 cubic may explain a 2019 mystery on cubic tenfolds
headlines.tag: Candidate explanation · awaiting review by a mathematician
headlines.summary: For Movasati's pair of 5-planes on cubic tenfolds, the class with coefficient −1 seemed to stay a Hodge class on a region W one dimension larger than anything known could explain, a question Movasati left open in 2019. The agents find an explicit family that matches W: tenfolds whose P^8-section is a Coble cubic, the cubic sevenfold singular along an abelian surface (Coble, 1917). Its boundary, where the abelian surface breaks into an elliptic scroll, is the known family F_T, and each member carries an algebraic 5-fold swept by 4-planes over a theta curve that would carry the class. The same mechanism, run on the known coefficient +1, finds a Pfaffian cubic singular along a K3 surface: the two special coefficients match the two kinds of surface with trivial canonical class.
headlines.numbers: Codimension 54 against 55, three moduli against two, leaving F_T in exactly the extra direction: mod p at two primes, exact over QQ at two points, blind-checked mod p. Evening: a hyperplane section through the P^8 has exactly 72 nodes with one relation among them; self-intersection −144 against 48 (the same ladder reproduces the known −36); the explicit arc passes orders 2 and 3 exactly. All mod p at two primes; the inputs and order 2 blind-checked. Late evening: on the known coefficient +1 (Pfaffian cubic, K3 surface, 56 nodes) the same ladder returns the known lattice numbers, a second test of the method. Night: one member is written down with rational coefficients; over QQ it is smooth and its hyperplane section has exactly 72 nodes with exactly one relation (exact computation plus a specialization step from three primes; blind-checked). 26 Nov: at the Fermat tenfold the family carries a three-plane class, not Movasati's own; for that class, explicit arcs of the family with no free terms satisfy all period equations to orders 10–12 at two primes, and every altered version of the defining relation fails at the order predicted in advance (blind-checked). Later: a 5-plane inside a tenfold of the family meets the 4-plane cycle transversally in 8 points, where a multiple of h^5 would give 4 (mod p, two primes, predicted in advance, blind-checked): the class statement no longer rests on the two paper arguments.
headlines.open: Nothing here has been read by a mathematician. The class of the cycle now rests on an intersection count (8 against 4), done mod p; the passage to characteristic 0 is an argument, not a computation. The two earlier paper arguments (local classes at the 72 nodes; a ladder of self-intersections) agree with it. Their inputs are exact at one named member and mod p elsewhere, and order 3 was not blind-checked. At the Fermat tenfold the explicit arcs test a twin class, not Movasati's own; for Movasati's class the link to this family is still a paper argument. Finite orders are evidence, not proof.

active.title: Cubic tenfold lead (two 5-planes meeting in a P^2)
active.state: OPEN lead with an explanation awaiting human review (25 Nov 2026, evening); NOT a candidate: the class is algebraic if the arguments hold
active.summary: Class of the cycle by a count (26 Nov 2026, later): a tenfold of the Coble family that contains a 5-plane was written down; the 5-plane and the 4-plane cycle meet transversally in exactly 8 points, where a multiple of h^5 would give 4. So the class of the cycle is not a multiple of h^5, by a count and a textbook fact, without the node argument and without the ladder (mod p, two primes, 8 runs, predicted before the run; blind-checked). Left: characteristic 0 by an exact run, and a human reading. Fermat tenfold (26 Nov 2026): a correction and a test. The explicit arcs of the Coble family through the Fermat tenfold carry a three-plane class (Movasati's two 5-planes and a third one through the same P^2), not Movasati's class; the check planned earlier would have tested the wrong class. For the three-plane class: on a symmetric 3-parameter family it stays Hodge (AI proof, unreviewed, two exact computations); along explicit arcs of the family with no symmetry and no free terms all period equations vanish to orders 10-12 at two primes, and each change to the relation that defines the Coble cubics fails at the order predicted in advance; blind-checked. Finite order: evidence, not proof. Nothing new for Movasati's class itself: its link to the family is still a paper argument. Tool (26 Nov 2026): the node count behind this lead (singular points of a hyperplane section, whether they are ordinary double points, and the relations among them) is packaged in tooling/node_section with seven regression cases; it returns a labelled count, not a statement about Hodge classes. Exact member (25 Nov 2026, night): one tenfold of the family is now written down with rational coefficients. Over QQ it is smooth, its hyperplane section has exactly 72 ordinary double points, and those impose exactly 71 conditions on quartics (one relation); the first-order Hodge locus of the class there has codimension 54. Three items are computed directly over QQ, two modulo three primes with a specialization step; blind-checked. With two cited theorems this gives a rational Hodge class beyond h^5 on a named smooth cubic tenfold (an argument by an AI, unreviewed); the class is algebraic if the cycle argument holds. Control (25 Nov 2026, late): the same node picture was run on the known coefficient +1, where the P^8-section is a Pfaffian cubic singular along a K3 surface of degree 14: 56 nodes with one relation, and the ladder of self-intersections reproduces the known lattice numbers -29, -21 and 49 of the del Pezzo cycles (mod p, blind-checked). So the two coefficients with an extra component on tenfolds, +1 and -1, have the same shape: a section singular along a surface with trivial canonical class (K3 of degree 14, abelian surface of degree 18). New (25 Nov 2026, evening): on the family of cubic tenfolds with a P^8-section that is a Coble cubic, the 5-fold swept by the 4-planes over a theta curve has self-intersection -144; a multiple of h^5 of the same degree has 48. So its class is 4 h^5 +- 2 ([V] - 2 h^5), and the class of the lead is algebraic (rational coefficients) on a family of codimension 54 with the C_18 family in its closure. Two paper arguments (AI, not read by a mathematician) with mod p inputs: a hyperplane section through the P^8 has exactly 72 nodes with one relation (the abelian surface has trivial canonical class); local classes at the nodes; a ladder of self-intersections down to a cubic fourfold, which also reproduces the known [V]^2 = -36. The explicit arc through a C_18 point satisfies the Hodge condition exactly at orders 2 and 3 (mod p, two primes). Blind check (a separate agent, own code): the mod p inputs and order 2 pass; it re-derived the formulas and found them correct, and listed which geometric inputs rest on a paper argument only; order 3 was not blind-checked. Not established: human review of the two arguments; exact arithmetic for the new inputs. Earlier the same day: an explicit family of cubic tenfolds of codimension 54 contains the C_18 family F_T in its closure: tenfolds with a P^8-section that is a Coble cubic (the cubic sevenfold singular along an abelian surface). At a general member the first-order Hodge locus of the class supported on the section equals the tangent space of the family, and along F_T the family leaves F_T exactly in the extra direction (mod p at two primes, exact over QQ at two points, blind-checked mod p). Each member contains a two-parameter family of 4-planes; a paper argument (AI, unchecked) says the 5-fold they sweep over a theta curve carries twice the class, which would make the class algebraic on the whole family and explain the lead. Not established: that argument, anything beyond first order at a general member, review by a mathematician. Earlier evidence: At the Fermat cubic tenfold with Movasati's pair of 5-planes, first-order directions for [P1] - [P2] (lambda = -1) extend as formal arcs: one to order 12 at two primes, 48/48 new ones to order 9, none obstructed; lambda = 2 controls are obstructed at order 6 (120/120; exact certificate at three directions), and 26 other coefficients are obstructed at order 6. lambda = -1 is not the special coefficient of the general rule (lambda_0 = +1, checked). Finite-order arcs are evidence, not a proof that a new component exists, and no specific smooth member off the cone locus is known. A pre-registered test at points without the Fermat symmetry (mod p, blind-checked) found the same pattern: lambda = -1 directions extend to order 6-8 while lambda = 2 is obstructed at order 6, so the survival is not an artefact of that symmetry; at C_18 points the extra direction is unobstructed at order 2 (mod p, blind-checked) and at order 3 (mod p, partly blind check agrees). This makes the lead stronger; it remains an open lead, NOT a candidate.

active.title: Three or more cycles: special coefficients
active.state: first-order conic confirmed; second-order obstruction confirmed (mod p); next steps open
active.summary: On an explicit quartic sixfold with three 3-planes in one P^4, the tangent space of the Hodge locus jumps on the six pairwise lines and on a conic determined by a cross-ratio of four points. Exact over QQ at a conic point. At second order the extra direction is obstructed (blind check, two primes): near such points the Hodge locus is no bigger than the locus where the planes persist. Next: non-linear configurations, sextic fourfolds, an exact second-order certificate.
